source: What happened? Each comparison returned either True or False. These are called boolean values (named after mathematician George Boole). When Python evaluates a comparison like 5 == 5, it checks if the statement is true or false and returns the corresponding boolean value. These True/False values are what Python uses to make decisions in if statements. Think of it like answering yes/no questions: "Is 5 equal to 5?" → True (yes), "Is 5 equal to 3?" → False (no).
